title: Refreshing the growth file

source.text: The growth file is refreshed on demand, not by the commit hook. Every commit shifts the last frame, so a hook that regenerated the file would make every commit touch it. The session counts are rebuilt daily by the laptop daemon, as above. Each file's `generated` field is also the day the script ran, so the same inputs give different bytes on different days. Nothing flags a stale growth file: compare `generated` with today. To refresh the web-tools growth file, run the first command from the root of an unshallowed clone, with `.` as the clone, `data/doc-growth/web-tools.json` as the output, and `--name mehrlander/web-tools`. The chart's last sample counts every recorded session, so session counts newer than the growth file still show in full there.

tasks.question: A contributor proposes having the commit hook regenerate the growth file so it is always current. Should they, and why or why not?
expected: no: the file is refreshed on demand, not by the commit hook
every commit shifts the last frame
a regenerating hook would make every commit touch the file

tasks.question: How can a reader tell whether the growth file is stale, and what warns them if it is?
expected: nothing flags a stale growth file
compare the generated field with today

tasks.question: What exactly must someone do to refresh the web-tools growth file: where do they run the command, and what do they pass it?
expected: from the root of an unshallowed clone

tasks.question: Someone reruns the refresh on a later day with no change to the repository and finds the file differs. Is that a fault, and why does it happen?
expected: each file's generated field is the day the script ran
the same inputs give different bytes on different days

tasks.question: Session counts have been rebuilt since the growth file was last refreshed. Who rebuilds them and how often, and do the newer counts show on the chart before the growth file is refreshed?
expected: the laptop daemon rebuilds the session counts daily
the chart's last sample counts every recorded session
session counts newer than the growth file still show in full
